title: Supported pseudo-coherent Ext is unchanged by completing coefficients
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $K\in D(A)$ a pseudo-coherent complex [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Put $E^i(K,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(K,M[i])$ for an ordinary $A$-module $M$ in degree zero. Fix an integer $a$. Assume that for every finite $A$-module $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], every $i\geq a$, and every prime $\mathfrak p$ not containing $I$, one has $E^i(K,M)_{\mathfrak p}=0$, where localization is [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For a finite $A$-module $N$ put $\widehat N=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}N/I^nN$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then for every $i\geq a$ the canonical $A$-linear maps
$$E^i(K,N)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{n\geq1}E^i(K,N/I^nN),\qquad E^i(K,N)\longrightarrow E^i(K,\widehat N)$$
are isomorphisms. The first map is induced by all quotient maps; the second is induced by $N\to\widehat N$. Both are natural in $N$.

source.place: Tag 0DYJ (lemma-ext-annihilated-into); Tag 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), case (3); Tag 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence). Finite-module support criterion and algebra.tex Tags 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), 031C (lemma-completion-complete).

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above finite free complex $P$ representing $K$ by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Finite free modules are projective: lift the finitely many basis vectors along an epimorphism. Thus [lem-sc-bounded-above-projective-kprojective] and [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] identify $E^i(K,M)$ naturally with degree-$i$ cohomology of $C(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,M[0])$. Indeed chain maps to $M[i]$ are the degree-$i$ cycles, and chain homotopies are boundaries (shift signs change a boundary only by a unit). In particular $C(M)^j=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-j},M)$, with differential $f\mapsto(-1)^{j+1}f d_P$. This construction is covariant in every module map $M\to M'$.

source.place: Tag 0DYI (lemma-ext-induced-toplogy), proof, finite-free Hom model; derived.tex Tag 064B (lemma-morphisms-from-projective-complex).

proof.text: For finite $M$, every $C(M)^j$ is finite, since a finite basis of $P^{-j}$ identifies it with a finite power of $M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], the cycles are finite; their quotient $H^i(C(M))$ is finite because images of generators generate a quotient. Fix $i\geq a$ and put $H=E^i(K,M)$. Its support lies in $V(I)$ by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], every prime containing $\operatorname{Ann}(H)$ contains $I$. The intersection-of-primes formula in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] gives $I\subseteq\sqrt{\operatorname{Ann}(H)}$. Noetherianity makes $I$ finitely generated, so [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] gives $I^tH=0$ for some $t\geq1$. Hence $H\to\widehat H=\varprojlim H/I^nH$ is an isomorphism: for $n\geq t$ the quotients are $H$ with identity transitions, and every compatible sequence is determined by its constant tail.

source.place: Tag 0DYJ (lemma-ext-annihilated-into), opening finiteness and power-annihilation argument; algebra.tex Tags 00IK, 00L2, 00E0 and 00IM.

proof.text: Fix finite $N$ and $i\geq a$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-short-complex-adic-cohomology-limit] to $C(N)^{i-1}\to C(N)^i\to C(N)^{i+1}$. Finite bases identify $C(N)^j/I^nC(N)^j$ with $C(N/I^nN)^j$: both are the same finite power of $N/I^nN$. The differential matrices reduce modulo $I^n$, so these identifications commute with differentials and quotient transitions. The lemma identifies $\widehat{E^i(K,N)}$ with $\varprojlim_nE^i(K,N/I^nN)$. Composing with Step 2 gives precisely the first map in the statement: coordinate $n$ sends a cycle to its image under $N\to N/I^nN$.

source.place: Tag 0EGU (lemma-consequence-Artin-Rees), assertion (2), applied to the three finite Hom modules.

proof.text: Put $Z=\ker(d:C(N)^i\to C(N)^{i+1})$, $B=\operatorname{im}(d:C(N)^{i-1}\to C(N)^i)$, $D=\operatorname{im}(d:C(N)^i\to C(N)^{i+1})$, and $H=Z/B$. These modules and $C(N)^{i+1}/D$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] and the generator argument for quotients. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] to $0\to Z\to C(N)^i\to D\to0$, $0\to D\to C(N)^{i+1}\to C(N)^{i+1}/D\to0$, $0\to B\to Z\to H\to0$, and $0\to\ker(d^{i-1})\to C(N)^{i-1}\to B\to0$. It follows that cycles of the termwise completed complex in degree $i$ are $\widehat Z$, its boundaries are $\widehat B$, and its cohomology is $\widehat H$. Finite bases give $\widehat{C(N)^j}=C(\widehat N)^j$: inverse limits of a fixed finite power are that power of the inverse limit, coordinate by coordinate. Matrix multiplication commutes with these coordinates, so the differentials agree. The induced map $H\to H^i(C(\widehat N))$ is $H\to\widehat H$, since it sends each cycle to its compatible quotient sequence. Step 2 makes it invertible. By Step 1 it is exactly the second map, induced by $N\to\widehat N$.

source.place: algebra.tex Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), assertion (2), and Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), assertion (2); finite-free Hom model from Tag 0DYI.

proof.text: For an $A$-linear map $N\to N'$, postcomposition gives a chain map $C(N)\to C(N')$. It commutes with every quotient projection and with completion: on a compatible sequence its $n$-th component is the induced map modulo $I^n$. Therefore both squares of the claimed maps commute on cycles and hence on cohomology; equality in the inverse limit is equality of all coordinates. These are $A$-linear maps throughout. This proves the asserted naturality.
